shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Cross-level combat, senses, NPC travel, CE bridge (experimental), "Traveler" climb animations, blueprint art, wall risers, research-gated links, a per-colony off switch, Perspective Shift + Toggleable Overlays support. Window 12 adds cross-level ability/jump targeting, band-aware range/target overlays, cross-level AI jumping, and §85 open-side arrivals on a 1x2 staircase with hand-tuned per-rotation art - none shipped, none tested.

Keep every ⚠.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> **⚠⚠ V1 SOURCE IS NOT GONE. DATED SOURCE BACKUPS LIVE AT `D:\Rimworld\As above, So below\<yyyymmdd-hhmmss>\Source\`** (ten snapshots, newest `20260726-154207`). These are `Source/` only - no Defs, no Textures. **When a V2 feature has a V1 ancestor, READ THE V1 FILE FIRST.** Confirmed useful: `Source/Stairs/ClimbAnimation.cs` (§78d). Tool boundary: `read` refuses that path, `bash`/`grep`/`sed` reach it fine.

# 0. START HERE

**CURRENT PHASE: BUILD MODE, WINDOW 12 OPEN. §85 IS BUILT AND AWAITING BOTH A TEST AND THE USER'S TAG PASS.**

**⚠⚠ WINDOW 12 IS FEATURE-COMPLETE APART FROM §85 AND UNSHIPPED. THE NEXT MOVE IS THE PUBLISH.** Four features: **§82** (targeting, #375), **§83** (overlays, #376), **§84** (AI jumping - downward #385, upward #386), all field-verified; **§85** (open-side arrivals + the 1x2 staircase + the east/west pin) builds green but has never run.

**WINDOW 11 IS SHIPPED** to Workshop 3776015553; pushed as **`93a8311`**.

**⚠ WORKSPACE DLL IS A DEBUG BUILD.** Re-run `dotnet build -c Release` in `Source/` before any publish.

**⚠ THE ONE THING NO WINDOW HAS EVER DONE: THE WORKSHOP SMOKE TEST.** Every verification, all thirteen windows, has been against the WORKSPACE copy; nobody has ever subscribed to the uploaded item and loaded it. A file that exists locally but was never uploaded would pass every check this project has ever made.

**⚠ OPEN, NOT URGENT:** **§85 TAG PASS** - the user has `Tools/LinkApproachTagger.html`; until they paste the export back, all 24 sprites run on derived defaults. **§85 IS BAKED AND PART-TESTED** - runs #387/#388: descents read correctly, the §85.14 side-approach bug was found and fixed (UNVERIFIED), and TWO ART-DIRECTION QUESTIONS ARE OPEN AND BLOCKING (§85.14 (a) the up-links' open edge, (b) ANSWERED, see §85.15). ⚠ (a) THE UP-LINK OPEN EDGE IS STILL OPEN AND STILL BLOCKING THE "they face south climbing upward" HALF OF THE REPORT. **§85.9 RESIDUAL ART DEFECT** - the east/west staircase sprites are now PINNED onto their footprint, but `AB_StairsUp_east/west` are the tall flight exported at a ~15-20 degree ROTATION (1.15 x 2.00 cells, diagonal) and no offset can fix that; redraw or one-rotating-graphic, user's call. **FINAL riser art** (Gemini PAUSED r5; ⚠ REWRITE prompts to the REAL palette - NO copper: power=steel+blue+hazard, pipe=pale+red valve, climate=ice+louver+orange, data=black+purple+cyan; the 12 shipped riser PNGs are placeholders by explicit user decision). **§77c ART** - grand staircase east/west sprites unrotated; user's domain. **ABOUT.XML DESCRIPTION IS STALE** (no research gating, no off switch, no AI jumping) - USER'S COPY, flagged not fixed. **`About/known-issues.json`** unchanged since window 8.

**⚠ SHIPPED KNOWINGLY UNVERIFIED (earlier windows):** §62.N, §70 (w8); §62.M, §66c, §66e (w7).

**⚠ USER WORKING RULES:** (1) NEVER source design ideas from other mods unless asked - scans COMPAT ONLY. **V1 is OUR OWN prior work and is exempt.** (2) Building art = USER via Nano Banana kits. (3) About.xml description = USER's copy. (4) N mockups = N CHOICES.

**What this mod is.** Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`, banded along +z. Priorities: visual clarity from above, performance, vanilla parity.

**⚠⚠ THE SIXTY-SIX RULES:** 1. CLAMP AT SELECTION. 2. NEVER PATCH `TryRebuildDirtyRegionsAndRooms`. 3. REGION CONNECTIVITY IS MORE OPTIMISTIC THAN THE PATHFINDER: flood CELLS. 4. COUNT EMITTERS/POPULATIONS/ENGINE STACKS. 5 (§48): A `Touch` TARGET IS USUALLY UNWALKABLE. 6 (§49): A VANILLA HELPER CAN BE A NO-OP INSTEAD OF AN ERROR. 7 (§52): THE CARVE IS NOT THE LAST WORD. 8 (§52.6): A LOAD-TIME REPAIR PASS MUST NEVER RE-CREATE WHAT THE PLAYER DELIBERATELY REMOVED. 9 (§53): SOME MISPLACEMENTS ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THE CELL. 10 (§54): A STRUCTURE IS NOT A CELL. 11 (§55): A CELL-LEVEL VERDICT CANNOT AUTHORIZE A PAWN-LEVEL ACTION. 12 (§56a): A FOREIGN MOD'S MAP-SIZE SNAPSHOT IS AN INPUT YOU CAN CORRECT. 13 (§56g): NEVER COPY A GRID YOU DID NOT WATCH BEING WRITTEN. 14 (§56m): BEFORE RELOCATING DATA, ASK WHAT IS ALREADY AT THE DESTINATION. 15 (§57i): ASSERT ALWAYS, NARRATE ON REQUEST. 16 (§56o): COUNT THE FOREIGN MOD'S WRITE PATHS. 17 (§56q): A PASSING RUN THAT DID NOT REPRODUCE THE FAILURE IS NOT A FIX. 18 (§57a): **NEVER EXONERATE A SUSPECT ON ONE CLEAN SAMPLE** - grep version at rule 54. 19 (§57f): `TicksGame` RESTARTS AT 0 EVERY NEW GAME. 20 (§57g): MOVING WORK EARLIER TURNS ON EVERY "IS THIS MAP READY" GATE. 21 (§58): THE PARALLEL GRIDS DO NOT TRAVEL WITH THE CONTENT. 22 (§59): A DERIVED GRID HAS NO PAWN IN IT. 23 (§60): AUDIT THE WEIGHTING, NOT THE SYMBOL. 24 (§61a): CLAMPING A VALUE WITHOUT CLAMPING ITS TARGET BUILDS AN OSCILLATOR. 25 (§61b): A POSTFIX ON `Update` IS AFTER THE OBJECT WAS ALREADY POSITIONED. 26 (§61f): EVERY READ OF THE MAP THE PLAYER CAN REACH MUST PASS THE RENDERER'S "IS IT DRAWN" GATE - selectable is drawable, and so is **highlightable** (§83). 27 (§62c): PREFER SPAWN/DESPAWN OVER FLICK. 28 (§63a): A PERMANENT FICTION INSTALLED FOR ONE SUBSYSTEM IS READ AS FACT BY EVERY OTHER ONE. 29 (§0b): REPORT OUTCOMES, NOT INTENTIONS. 30 (§66d): A FELT DURATION IS A CHAIN, NOT A NUMBER. 31 (§66f): MAKE THE GUARD SAY WHICH CLAUSE DECLINED. 32 (§69a): TURNING OFF A TICK TURNS OFF EVERY SERVICE THAT RODE ON IT. 33 (§62k): A FILTER THAT CAN REJECT EVERYTHING MUST SAY SO. 34 (§62l): AN INVISIBLE THING IS ABSENT FROM EVERY SECTION LAYER. 35 (§62n): A CLONED FOREIGN DEF MADE VISIBLE IS IN NONE OF THE HOST'S OWN LOOKUPS. 36 (§70a): RUN VANILLA'S OWN LEGALITY PREDICATE. 37 (§71a): NAME THE ENFORCEMENT POINT BEFORE NAMING THE SYMPTOM. 38 (§73): WHEN A SPRITE MUST APPEAR AWAY FROM ITS THING'S POSITION, OWN THE DRAW - **and §84.8's other half: when a thing insists on drawing itself at a position of its OWN, the offset must be applied to THAT position, not to the one you pass it.** 39 (§76): WINNING THE LAST WRITE DOES NOT SETTLE A DISAGREEMENT ABOUT THE TARGET. 40 (§75.h): A TRIPWIRE THAT FIRES BEFORE THE OBSERVER ATTACHES IS NOT A TRIPWIRE. 41 (§77a): A STRUCT FIELD YOU NEVER SET IS A FEATURE YOU NEVER SHIPPED. 42 (§77b): THE DIRECTION A MOTION READS AS IS A PROPERTY OF THE THING, NOT OF THE ARRIVAL. 43 (§78): **DEFER THE MOVE, NEVER THE DECISION.** 44 (§78b): AN OFFSET APPLIED WHOLE ON FRAME ONE IS A TELEPORT. 45 (§78d): **A DIRECTION OF TRAVEL IS NOT A DIRECTION OF ELEVATION.** 46 (§78d): **NON-UNIFORM SCALE x ROTATION = SHEAR.** 47 (§79): **A FOREIGN MOD'S CACHED CURSOR CELL IS AN ASSUMPTION ABOUT COORDINATE SPACE.** 48 (§81a): **A WRITE THAT IS READ BACK BY ITS OWN CALLER IS NOT A WRITE.** 49 (§0c): **A TEST THAT PROVES FEATURE A SAYS NOTHING ABOUT FEATURE B.** 50 (§82a): **TWO OF OUR OWN PATCHES ON ONE VANILLA METHOD CANCEL SILENTLY.** GREP OUR OWN `[HarmonyPatch]` LIST FOR THE TARGET METHOD FIRST. 51 (§82b): **A FACTORY HAS USUALLY CONSUMED ITS INPUT BY THE TIME THE POSTFIX RUNS.** 52 (§83a): **AN OVERLAY MUST ASK THE SAME QUESTION THE CLICK WILL ASK, AND IT MUST NOT BE A QUESTION THAT WRITES.** 53 (§83c): **A PREDICATE PASSED IN IS CLOSED OVER THE ARGUMENTS THE CALLER ALREADY HAS.** 54 (§84a): **A CLEAN GREP IS NOT AN ABSENCE - SEARCH FOR THE CAPABILITY, NOT THE TYPE NAME.** 55 (§84.3): **"AFTER THE DUTY HAD ITS TURN" INCLUDES A FALLBACK JOB YOU WOULD NEVER CALL A REAL ONE.** Symptom: a JobGiver perfect when invoked directly, never firing in play, with `curJob=Wait_Wander` and a live duty. 56 (§84.5): **WHEN YOU RANK CANDIDATES BY ONE COST AND FILTER THEM BY ANOTHER, THE RANKING FINDS THE FILTER'S BLIND SPOT.** Spend the surcharge on the SEARCH RADIUS, not on the validity test - and note that widening the search makes it WORSE, which is the trap. 57 (§85a): **WHEN TWO SUBSYSTEMS EACH ANSWER "WHICH SIDE OF THIS THING", ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT TO BE WRONG.** Departures had derived the open edge since §78c; arrivals never asked, and the bug hid for eight windows because both answers were individually defensible. Give the question ONE owner. 58 (§85b): **A PROPERTY OF THE ART CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE DEF.** When the sprite and its rotation disagree (§77c), only a human looking at the PNG can arbitrate - build the tagging tool instead of the cleverer heuristic. 59 (§85.8): **`size` MUST BE MEASURED FROM THE DRAWING, NOT COPIED FROM `drawSize`.** They are different questions ("what do pawns walk on" vs "how big is the picture"), and matching them is a plausible-looking guess that silently buys empty cells - here, two cells of pure door that arrivals were then set down in. 60 (§85.9): **MEASURE THE PIXELS; AND A DRAW OFFSET AND AN ART-OFFSET TABLE ARE THE SAME NUMBER TWICE.** `Tools/MeasureSprites.ps1` reproduces the whole hand-made `ArtOffsets` table to two decimals in one call - so "shrinking the footprint made the art hang off" is answerable exactly instead of by eye. And the moment a sprite is PINNED with `drawOffsetEast/West`, its row in a "where is the art really drawn" table becomes ZERO; leaving the old transcription in double-counts the correction. 61 (§85c): **A COLOURED VERSION OF A GRAPHIC IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT, AND VANILLA HARD-CODES ITS TYPE.** `Graphic_Multi.GetColoredVersion` returns `GraphicDatabase.Get<Graphic_Multi>` - so a subclass silently degrades for every STUFFED thing, which is every one that is actually on the map, while the unstuffed def in the inspector looks perfect. 62 (§85d): **A TABLE OF FINISHED ANSWERS ROTS; STORE ONLY WHAT NOTHING ELSE OWNS AND DERIVE THE REST.** Split by WHO OWNS THE INPUT - a measurement of the art belongs to the PNG, an offset and a size belong to the def - then compute. The old hand-kept table had been wrong about the ladder for as long as the ladder existed, because nothing said its def offsets and its art offsets were the same number. 63 (§85.14): **MEASURE A PATIENCE FROM THE EVENT IT NAMES.** A backstop timer started at the wrong event does not fail loudly - it silently becomes "always fire", and it works perfectly in every close-up test because the timer has not expired yet. Read the constant's own banner against the field it reads: "two seconds after getting CLOSE" and `now - startedTick` are not the same clock. 64 (§85.16): **A DIAGNOSTIC THAT IS OFF BY DEFAULT IS A DIAGNOSTIC THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** Three runs in a row were spent reasoning about code because the trace flag defaulted to false and nobody remembered the dev action. Gate verbosity on the BUILD (`#if DEBUG`), not on a human's memory - the test build should incriminate itself. 65 (§85.17): **WHEN A DERIVED RULE IS RIGHT THREE TIMES OUT OF FOUR, THE FOURTH IS NOT A DIFFERENT RULE - IT IS A DEFECTIVE INPUT.** Do not re-derive the whole table to fit the outlier; set the outlier by hand and say so. And note the corollary that hid this for four windows: an outlier that agrees with the default in 3 of 4 orientations gets reported once, vaguely, by whoever happens to build it facing the wrong way. 66 (§85.19): **A DESTINATION CELL DOES NOT CONSTRAIN THE SIDE IT IS ENTERED FROM.** RimWorld pathing has no approach direction, so "make the pawn come in through the opening" cannot be expressed as a destination - it needs TWO legs: walk to the tile in front, then one cardinal step in. And when you add a second leg, check every trigger that fires on "the pawn stopped": finishing leg one IS a stop, so any stopped-short backstop will steal the crossing unless the new leg is tested first.

# 85. OPEN-SIDE ARRIVALS, THE APPROACH TAGGER, THE 1x2 STAIRCASE, THE EAST/WEST PIN — **BUILT, NEVER RUN**

`Source/V2/ABLinkApproach.cs` (new), `ABWormholePather.LandingCell`/`ApproachLanding`/`EntryCellFor`, `ABStairAnim.NotifyCarried` + `ArtOffsets`, `ABBandStairsExt.approachCells`, `Defs/V2/AB2_Stairs.xml` (sizes + draw offsets), `Tools/LinkApproachTagger.html`, `Tools/MeasureSprites.ps1` (new).

**⚠⚠ 85a THE DEFECT (rule 57).** Field report with a screenshot: a pawn coming down a staircase should be set down on **the tile in front of whichever way the stairs open**, "instead of on the sides or inside of the building", because with door path costs an arrival parked on the building stalls there and a side arrival reads as walking through a handrail. Cause: **departures had owned this question since §78c and arrivals had never been asked it.** `LandingCell` preferred `far.Position` - a cell INSIDE a multi-cell `Building_Door` - and fell back to `CellFinder.TryFindRandomCellNear`, i.e. the sides.

**85.2 ONE OWNER.** `ABLinkApproach.TryGet` returns `{mouth, outside, outward, tagged}` and is now the single answer for the entry cell, the landing cell and the emerge anchor. Its derived fallback is the old `EntryCellFor` edge math verbatim (`Rotation.Opposite`, `CellRect.CenterCell` along that edge), so an untagged def behaves exactly as it did.

**⚠⚠ 85b THE TABLE, AND WHY IT IS HAND-TAGGED (rule 58).** The open side is a property of the PNG. §77c records that some sprites disagree with their own rotation. `Tools/LinkApproachTagger.html` shows all 24 sprites (6 directional defs x 4 rotations) over their real footprint plus a one-cell ring, the user clicks the landing tile, and it exports `<approachCells>` blocks. **⚠ The west cards for grand stairs and both ladders render `_east` MIRRORED** (`Graphic_Multi.Init` sets `westFlipped` when no `_west` PNG exists) **and the stair cards apply the §85.9 draw offsets** - the tool must show what the game draws, not what the folder contains. Keep its `DEFS` table in sync with the defs by hand; there is no import.

**85.3 THE TAG FORMAT.** `List<IntVec2>` on `ABBandStairsExt`, 4 entries in Rot4 order, each `(dx,dz)` from the footprint's **SOUTH-WEST corner**, naming a cell exactly one step OUTSIDE one edge. SW-corner-relative on purpose: `Position` is not the geometric centre of an even-sized building (`GenAdj.AdjustForRotation`). A tag that is interior, diagonal or two cells out is REFUSED (not clamped) and the derived default is used.

**85.4 THE LANDING ORDER** (`ApproachLanding`): tagged outside tile → the rest of that outside edge, working outwards → the mouth cell → the rest of the open edge on the footprint → then, and only then, the old anchor-then-random-near chain. **⚠ STANDABLE OUTSIDE, WALKABLE ON THE FOOTPRINT** - the link is `PassThroughOnly`, so `Standable` is false for every cell of its own footprint (the §78c trap), while outside the footprint a walkable-not-standable cell is somebody else's doorway. Every candidate is also `SameBand` as the anchor.

**85.5 THE EMERGE ANCHOR IS THE MIDDLE OF THE OPEN EDGE, NOT OF THE BUILDING.** `ABLinkApproach.MouthPoint` = `TrueCenter + outward * (extent/2 - 0.5)`; identical to `TrueCenter` for a 1x1 ladder, half a cell out on the 1x2 stairs, one cell on the grand stairs.

**85.6 HOW TO TEST IT.** Banded run; build a staircase and send a colonist down. They must appear on the tile in front of the opening and step off it, not stand on the art. Repeat rotated all four ways (architect menu - the dev action always spawns Rot4.North), then a 3x3 grand staircase and a ladder. Crowd case: 3-4 pawns at once, queueing in front rather than stacking or scattering. **Also check the 1x2 footprint and the east/west pin** - place ghost, blueprint and built thing must all show the art on the building.

**⚠⚠ 85.8 THE 1x2 STAIRCASE (rule 59).** User: "fix the normal staircases to be 2x1, the grand staircases are fine". Measured: `AB_StairsDown_south` 0.84 x 1.48 cells, `AB_StairsUp_south` 0.83 x 1.67 - a single narrow flight, NOT a 2x2 block. The old `<size>(2,2)</size>` was itself a correction (originally drawSize with no size, so a drawn 2x2 sat on ONE cell) that **overshot by copying `drawSize` instead of measuring the drawing**, buying two cells of pure door - exactly what §85a was setting arrivals down in. Now `<size>(1,2)</size>`, authored NORTH so the long axis is the RUN axis; `GenAdj` swaps it for east/west. **⚠ `drawSize` STAYS (2,2)** - a picture size, not a footprint. Six cardinal approach cells instead of eight. **Everything else was already footprint-generic** (`OccupiedRect` throughout: carve, apron, fog flood, cell pairing, place worker); the one note is `ABWormhole.TryCellPairs`, whose shape guard said "every link def is square today" and is now live - pairs stay safe only because both ends share a def size AND the counterpart is spawned with THIS end's Rotation. **SAVE COMPAT:** size is not scribed, so old 2x2 stairs reload as 1x2 at the same Position and Rotation; both ends shrink identically, and a shrink cannot overlap anything.

**⚠⚠ 85.9 THE EAST/WEST PIN, AND THE ART DEFECT UNDERNEATH IT (rule 60).** Predicted when §85.8 landed, then field-reported off the tagger: "east and west stairs need adjusted". `Tools/MeasureSprites.ps1` (new - PowerShell + `System.Drawing`, since Modmixer ships no imagemagick/PIL) gave exact alpha boxes, **and reproduced every row of the hand-made `ArtOffsets` table to two decimals**, which validates both the tool and the old measurements:

| sprite | size (cells) | centre offset |
|---|---|---|
| `AB_StairsDown_east` | 1.24 x 1.17 | (-0.109, +0.414) |
| `AB_StairsDown_west` | 1.24 x 1.16 | (+0.109, +0.418) |
| `AB_StairsUp_east` | 1.15 x **2.00** | (-0.156, 0.000) |
| `AB_StairsUp_west` | 1.15 x **2.00** | (+0.156, 0.000) |

APPLIED: `drawOffsetEast`/`drawOffsetWest` on both `graphicData` and `blueprintGraphicData` of both stair defs, negating those centre offsets. `Verse.Graphic` applies `DrawOffsetForRot` on the `Print` path (line ~316, the `MapMeshOnly` path these use) AND on `DrawWorker` (line ~279, ghosts/blueprints), so one pair of numbers covers built, blueprint and ghost. **⚠ In 1.6 `DrawOffsetForRot` is a plain switch with NO auto-mirroring - west must be stated.** **⚠ The matching `ArtOffsets` east/west rows are now ZERO by construction; re-adding the transcriptions would double-count the pin.**

**⚠⚠ 85.12 THE BAKE LANDED, AND ABStairAnim's ART TABLE IS NOW DERIVED (rule 62).** The user's tagger export was applied by script to all six defs: four `drawOffset<Rot>` in `graphicData` AND `blueprintGraphicData`, an `ABLinkArtExt.drawSizes` block, and an explicit `approachCells` block. **Every approach cell came back at the derived default** - the notch edge was right all along - so §85's tagging changed no behaviour and is now explicit DATA instead of inferred, immune to a future change in the derivation. What the user actually moved was the ART: e.g. `AB2_StairsDown` east `(-0.25, 0, -0.35)` where §85.9's arithmetic pin had said `(+0.109, 0, -0.414)`, and east/west size `(2, 1.9)`. **A measured centring and a chosen composition are not the same answer, and the human one wins** - the pin centred the alpha box, the user aligned the drawn MOUTH with the landing tile.

**⚠⚠ 85d THE LATENT BUG THE BAKE EXPOSED (rule 62).** `ABStairAnim.ArtOffsets` was a hand-written table of FINISHED ANSWERS - one Vector2 per def per rotation, meaning "where the art is drawn relative to the cell". It duplicated data the defs already own, so it had to be re-measured by hand whenever an offset or size changed, and **it had already silently rotted**: `AB2_LadderUp`'s north and south rows were `(0,0)` while the def has carried `drawOffsetNorth/South` of -0.33 / +0.33 since V1. The ladder's climb clip had been anchored a third of a cell off its own art for as long as the ladder has existed, and nobody re-derived the table when those offsets were added, because nothing said they were the same number.

Replaced by `ArtBoxCentre` + a derived `ArtOff(link)`. The split is the only one that survives editing: **the ART BOX is a property of the PNG** (fractions of the image, changing only on a redraw) while **OFFSET and SIZE are properties of the DEF** (changing whenever the tool is used). So only the box is stored, and `ArtOff` computes `GraphicData.DrawOffsetForRot(rot) + box * ABLinkArt.DrawSizeFor(def, rot)` at call time - the same `DrawOffsetForRot` call `Verse.Graphic` itself makes, so the clip cannot disagree with the screen. **Fractions, not cells, is what makes the box immune to a draw-size change.** Re-run `Tools/MeasureSprites.ps1 -CellsX 1 -CellsZ 1` after any redraw and paste the "centre offset" column straight in.

**85.13 THE TOOL IS RE-SEEDED TO THE SHIPPED STATE.** `DEFS[].off` and the new `DEFS[].siz` in the tagger now carry the baked values, so "reset" means "back to what is in the defs" and the amber "edited" flag means "differs from shipped". **⚠ RE-SEED IT AFTER EVERY BAKE** or the tool quietly invites the user to redo work that is already done. `ABLinkArt`'s registry also warns when it registers nothing (rule 33) - a typo in the `Class` attribute fails silently at def load and would read as "the overdraw bake never applied".

**⚠⚠ 85.14 "THEY CAN STILL APPROACH FROM THE SIDES" - THE PATIENCE WAS MEASURED FROM THE WRONG EVENT (rule 63).** Field report against the baked build, on the grand staircase. The carry trigger in `TickTransits` is `nearEnough && (onEntry || stoppedShort || outOfPatience)`, and `outOfPatience` read `now - t.startedTick > 120` - **`startedTick` is when the transit RECORD WAS MADE, i.e. when the pawn was ordered**, while the constant's own banner said "within two seconds of GETTING CLOSE". Any pawn more than ~7 cells from the stairwell therefore arrived with the patience ALREADY expired and was carried on the first tick it came within `ArriveRadius` (3) of the anchor - from whatever side it was walking past, having never reached its entry cell. §78c's walk-onto-the-treads was therefore only ever working for pawns that started next to the stairs, which is exactly how it was always tested.

**⚠ WORST ON THE BIGGEST FOOTPRINT, WHICH IS WHY THE GRAND STAIRCASE IS WHERE IT WAS SEEN.** `ArriveRadius` is measured from the ANCHOR: on a 3x3 the anchor is the centre cell, so a radius of 3 covers the whole building plus a ring outside it, and a pawn detouring around to the mouth is "close" for the entire detour. On a 1x2 the same bug exists but the geometry hides it.

FIX: `Transit.nearSinceTick` (0 = not yet close), stamped on the first tick the pawn is within `ArriveRadius`, deferred out of the `pending` enumeration through `tmpStamp` because `Transit` is a struct in a Dictionary and cannot be updated in place. Patience raised **120 -> 300** as well, because the unit is the FOOTPRINT, not the cell: walking around a 3x3 is ~8 cells (~1.7s) before the mouth is even reachable. The ceiling is cheap because `stoppedShort` still fires instantly whenever the pawn is genuinely blocked - the "delayed, never denied" guarantee (rule 43) is untouched, only re-based.

With the mouth at `Opposite(Rotation)`, a south-facing stairs-up is entered at its NORTH cell and slides south, so the facing is south. Flipping `AB2_StairsUp`/`AB2_GrandStairsUp` to open on the ROTATION side would make the climb start at the south end and travel north, and is *physically* the more coherent model (one staircase, two ends, opposite edges - the pawn keeps its direction of travel across the level change instead of reversing). **⚠ BUT THE SAME TABLE PLACES THE EMERGE WHEN DESCENDING**, and the user reports every descent as correct today - so a blind flip trades a reported bug for an unreported one. Both need one confirmation before touching.

**⚠⚠ 85.15 ONE CLIMB GRAMMAR, INVERTED ONLY IN THE VERTICAL (user's spec).** "I want ascent to recede like they're disappearing from view due to being on the level above. Four constants collapsed to two (`ClimbRecede` 0.28, `EmergeAppear` 0.18) and the collapse IS the feature - one number per half is what makes the directions match. ⚠ The descent emerge changed too (it used to start 12% LARGE, now 18% small); the user called descents good before this, so that half is the one to watch on the next run.

**THE WALK IS NOW TWO LEGS.** `Transit.approachCell` (the tile in FRONT of the opening, from `ABLinkApproach.outside`, resolved by the new `ApproachCellFor`) is leg one's destination; on arrival the sweep issues a one-cell `StartPath` onto the mouth, which is cardinal and can therefore only enter through the opening. `legTwo` latches so it fires once.

**⚠⚠ THE ORDERING TRAP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS NEEDED CARE:** a pawn finishing leg one STOPS, so `stoppedShort` is TRUE on that very tick and the old trigger block would carry it from the approach tile - one cell short of the art, i.e. the bug wearing a new hat. The leg-two branch is therefore tested BEFORE the triggers and `continue`s past them for that tick. **⚠ IT IS STILL NOT A GATE (rule 43):** the record stays pending, the patience clock keeps running, and a failed or blocked leg two is carried from wherever the pawn stands by `stoppedShort` / `outOfPatience` on a later tick. Delay, never denial.

**⚠ HANDLED ON BOTH TRIGGERS.** `TryConsumeArrival` needs the same branch, because a pawn ordered while ALREADY on the approach tile gets `dest == its own position` and vanilla's "already there" branch fires `PatherArrived` synchronously - the sweep never sees an intermediate tick. This is distinguishable from the §33c re-segmentation loop because a real one-cell path to a DIFFERENT cell is issued before the arrival is consumed, and `legTwo` caps it at one. Reciprocally, `ApproachCellFor` returns Invalid when the pawn is ALREADY on the mouth, so it is never sent out to the front tile to walk back in - that is an oscillation, refused rather than tolerated (rule 24).

Transient occupancy is deliberately NOT tested in `ApproachCellFor` - a pawn standing there does not make it the wrong tile, it makes a queue. UNVERIFIED.
